rpc: add get_node_info with operational metrics counters
Contributed by Ziyang (as exfer-stack) upstream to ahuman-exfer/exfer, the Exfer chain itself.
https://github.com/ahuman-exfer/exfer/pull/41

The node exposes height and tip but nothing about its operational health, so reliability work — orphan-rate soaks especially — is currently judged by grepping unstructured logs. This adds a read-only `get_node_info` method plus the monotonic counters the orphan-rate roadmap's "measurement first" section calls for, so health is queryable and the next soak can read hard numbers instead of log lines.

## `get_node_info`

New method, purely additive — no existing method's response changed. Returns:

- `version` (RELEASE_TAG), `network`, `genesis_block_id` (same source as `get_block_height`, never tip-derived)
- `tip_height`, `tip_block_id`, `tip_age_seconds`
- `peer_count`, `mempool_size`, `mempool_bytes`, `uptime_seconds`
- `metrics`: `blocks_accepted`, `blocks_orphaned`, `reorgs_applied`, `total_blocks_undone`, `retrying_reorg_trigger` (the deep-fork live-lock canary), `reorg_recoverable_errors`, `reorg_fatal_errors`, `rate_cap_disconnects`, `rate_cap_softdrops`, `global_block_drops`, `channel_send_drops`

Those last three gate criteria — orphan/stale proxy (`blocks_orphaned`), reorg-apply error level (`reorg_recoverable_errors`/`reorg_fatal_errors`), and the live-lock canary (`retrying_reorg_trigger`) — are exactly the signals the PR #34 release-gate soak was checking by hand.

## Non-invasive by construction

Every counter is a `Relaxed` `AtomicU64::fetch_add`, `#[inline]`, lock-free, placed beside the existing log line at its event site in `sync.rs`. No counter gates a branch; nothing in consensus, validation, fork-choice, relay, ordering, or any wire/RPC response shape changes. `RELEASE_TAG` moved into `types` so the library-crate RPC and the binary `--version` share one definition (it was binary-only, so the RPC would otherwise have reported the `0.1.0` Cargo placeholder).

Deferred: per-stage latency histograms (receive→PoW-verified→connected→relayed) need timing threaded through the block pipeline rather than a single atomic at a discrete event — documented in the module header.

## Verification

- `cargo test` and `cargo test --features testnet`: green (3 metrics unit tests + 2 `get_node_info` RPC-shape/activity integration tests, full suites 0 failed).
- Live devnet node, real JSON-RPC: `get_node_info` returns `version` 1.12.0, `network` devnet, advancing `tip_height` with small `tip_age_seconds` and growing `uptime`, counters reading cleanly; `get_block_height` byte-identical to before. (Reorg-counter increments over live RPC couldn't be exercised on a solo isolated devnet — no second peer to fork against — but the unit/integration tests drive those counters directly.)

Deployable plain `cargo build --release` builds green; the new method is useful for fleet observability independent of the soak.
